newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty firms on dollar slip, depos inch up.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty firms on dollar slip, depos inch up.

text.p: The Polish zloty strenghtened slightly versus the basket of currencies as the U.S. dollar sliped against the mark, but trade was slow on Friday as players were reluctant to open speculative positions.
Dealers expected low activity on Friday ahead of the long weekend due to Poland's Independence Day on Monday and different spot value dates for dollar/mark and dollar/zloty.
"The session should be quiet today, opened dollar/mark positions should be closded today because of different value dates," said Wojciech Czajkowski of Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA.
At the 0940 GMT the zloty was quoted at 2.09/2.04 percent from the trading band centre, up from opening's 2.01/1.91 percent from parity.
It was quoted at 2.8115/30 to the dollar, up from opening's 2.8150/75 and at 1.8603/13 to the mark against 1.8610/30.
Polish markets close on Monday for Independence Day Holiday and today's value date is November 13, 1996.

On the money market one-day deposit rates inched up after recent central bank drainages cleared surpluses and dealers singalled that there may be some cash shortages next week as tomorrow/next rates increased today.
"It seems there is no money in tomorrow/next deposits," said Malgorzata Sikora from ING Bank in Warsaw.
At 0950 GMT, overnight deposits were quoted at 19.15/19.35 percent, up at bid from opening's 19.10/19.35 percent.
Tomorrow/next depos were at 19.20/19.40 percent, up from 19.10/19.35 percent.
Three-month depos were bid at 19.45 percent, nearly a point above the comparable 13-week T-bill, last sold with an average yield of 18.55 percent on the primary market.
